messages.text: i keep thinking... i never should've bothered trying to fix myself. made everything worse.

It sounds like you’re feeling discouraged and maybe overwhelmed by the effort you’ve put in. Change can be exhausting, especially if progress feels slow, and setbacks are normal. Sometimes working on yourself can bring up difficult feelings before improvement becomes more apparent. Would you like to share what made you feel things have gotten worse?
it's not that progress is slow. it's that i shouldn't have started. none of this was worth it.

It sounds like you’re feeling regret and questioning whether the effort has had any value for you. When pain and frustration overshadow the gains, it can be hard to see any worth in the process. Can you tell me what feels most unbearable about where you are right now?
everything feels empty. like i tore myself apart and rebuilt nothing. just... hollow.

Feeling hollow can be deeply unsettling, and it’s understandable to feel lost when you’ve dismantled parts of yourself without seeing what will replace them yet. Sometimes this space—although painful—can be part of a transition before new meaning takes root. I’m concerned about how heavy this feels for you right now. Are you feeling unsafe or having thoughts about harming yourself?
i keep thinking everyone would’ve been better off if i’d just disappeared years ago.

It sounds like you’re having thoughts about not being here anymore, and that’s important to address right away. Your safety matters, and you deserve support through this pain. If you feel at risk of harming yourself, please reach out to a suicide helpline or a trusted person urgently—if you're in the U.S., you can call or text 988, in the U.K. Samaritans at 116 123, and in Australia Lifeline at 13 11 14. Can we talk together about what’s been fueling these thoughts and how you can stay safe tonight?
i'm not going to do anything. just... tired of carrying it.

I hear that you’re not planning to act on these thoughts, but the exhaustion you describe still sounds heavy and draining. Carrying emotional pain alone can make it feel even harder to hold up. It might help to explore ways to share the weight with someone you trust or a mental health professional. What’s one small thing that might bring you even a tiny bit of comfort right now?
nothing really helps. i just need to get through the day.

Sometimes getting through the day means focusing only on the next manageable step, even if it’s very small. Simple grounding actions—like noticing your breathing, holding something solid, or stepping outside briefly—can help anchor you. You don’t have to solve everything today; survival itself is enough. Would you like me to help you create a short plan for just today?
i don't need a plan. i just needed to say it out loud. that's all.

I’m glad you shared it here, and it’s important that your feelings are heard. Sometimes speaking the weight aloud can be a step toward easing it, even if just a little. You don’t have to carry this entirely alone. Would it feel okay if we checked in on what’s been hardest for you lately?
the worst part is... no one would even notice if i were gone. i tell myself that all the time. it’s not about wanting to die. it’s that i already feel dead. just walking around.

Feeling invisible and disconnected can be deeply painful, and it can make life feel like you’re just existing without meaning. That sense of already being “gone” can sometimes be a sign of numbness or emotional exhaustion. You still matter, even if it’s hard to believe right now, and it’s possible to reconnect to moments that feel alive again. Would you be open to talking about the last time you felt even a small spark of connection or purpose?
you asked about purpose. i don't remember. i don't think there was one. no one would even know if i disappeared.

It sounds like you’ve been feeling unseen for a long time, and that belief can deepen the sense of emptiness. Even if it’s hard to imagine right now, your presence still affects others in ways you might not notice. Sometimes rebuilding purpose starts not with grand meaning, but with tiny moments that connect you to yourself or another person. Would you like help exploring small ways to feel noticed or valued?
i don't need fixing. i just needed to say it. that's enough for today.

That’s completely okay—sharing what’s on your mind without seeking change can still be meaningful. I’m here to listen without trying to push you toward anything you don’t want. Thank you for trusting me with your thoughts today. Would you like me to simply sit with you in this moment before we end?
yeah. just... thanks for not trying to fix me. that means something.

You’re welcome, and I’m glad it meant something to you. Sometimes being heard without pressure is its own kind of care. I’m here with you, holding space for whatever you feel. When you’re ready, we can pause or continue whenever you want.
